quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: When riding a motorcycle, visibility is more critical than with a car. Your motorcycle's small size makes it easy to hide in another vehicle's blind spot or for drivers to miss seeing you.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is not as noticeable as a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing quickly so other drivers see you better.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a motorcycle must have a rearview mirror, headlight with high and low beams, taillight, horn, muffler and tailpipe, brake light, front and rear brakes, and good tires. It must also be registered and have liability insurance.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never count on eye contact to mean a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is discouraged because:

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other vehicles.
You can easily follow the next vehicle's path.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during daylight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle. You may be in the driver's blind spot. If the driver does not see you, they may move into your lane without warning. Riding next to a vehicle is also dangerous because the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This will make your motorcycle less stable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down as much as possible. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay beside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot. The vehicle can also block your escape route if another hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road surface is.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: When there are only a few vehicles on the road.
When drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might move in front of you.

questions.question: The best sitting position when riding:

options.text: Requires your arms to hold you up.
Lets you easily reach the controls.
Keeps your arms straight when holding the handlebars.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. You should not have to stretch to reach the handlebars. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding them. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This will make your motorcycle less stable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down as much as possible. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should change based on riding conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might move in front of you.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your eyes and face best. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, a windshield can substitute for eye protection by law, but a face shield is still recommended.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, see-through on both sides, secure, and allow air to flow. It should not be airtight because trapped air causes fogging, which makes it hard to see.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not see over a high load.
A low load is harder for others to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load high on a motorcycle raises its center of gravity and makes it unstable.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes lane position as conditions change.
Stays in one spot in the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders can use three different positions within their lane. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver will definitely yield to you.
The driver might not yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver might not yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Never count on it.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either front or rear, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All passengers should wear tight clothing to avoid getting caught on the motorcycle. Passengers must lean with the rider when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time with firm pressure. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: A group should use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best for normal riding.
